transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-11-24 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Hydra CTO), Liam Cross (Hydra Lead ML), Sofia Mendes (Hydra Platform)
--- Automated Summary (may be rough) ---
Hydra currently building a streaming chat layer for their customer support bot. They need p95 guarantees at low latency for conversational streaming and are weighing hosted vs dedicated vs private. They asked for benchmark scripts, perf matrix and security docs.
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - im Maya, AE on Redwood, and Jonah our SE will take tech lead on perf stuff.
00:16 Priya Rao: Hi, thanks. we're trying to understand if we can keep the streaming experience snappy at scale. our SLO is p95 under 200ms for token streaming in production, which is kinda ambitious i know.
00:30 Jonah Patel: right. quick clarifying q: is that 200ms per token or for end-to-end chunk latency? and what model family are you planning to run?
00:45 Liam Cross: good point. target is per-token streaming latency as observed from our web socket edge to the first token arriving. for models we are evaluating a mix of open LLMs and some 7B-13B variants; we also have interest in Redwood's catalog suggestions.
01:03 Sofia Mendes: traffic profile: normal concurrency about 200 active sessions, each session averages 4 tokens/sec while typing; bursts during campaigns can get to ~2000 concurrent for ~10-15 minutes.
01:28 Maya Chen: okay that's helpful. so two parts: steady-state p95 at 200 conc, and burst handling to 2k. for steady-state, we generally can hit low p95s on dedicated pools tuned for streaming, less predictable on hosted depending on region and load.
01:46 Priya Rao: so potentially we need Dedicated? also curious about private/VPC for data controls — we have some regs around residency.
01:58 Jonah Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, so lower tail variance; plus you can configure autoscale and burst capacity. private deploy is an option if you need customer-managed network and KMS. a couple of caveats: private infra introduces ops overhead and we'll need specifics on your cluster/hardware.
02:18 Liam Cross: can you quantify "lower tail variance"? like examples or numbers? we ran a quick internal perf and p95 jumped to 1s during cold cache events.
02:32 Jonah Patel: yeah cold-starts and KV-cash misses — sorry, KV cache — can spike. with prefix/KV cache enabled and warm KV, we've seen p95 drop from ~800-1200ms down to ~120-180ms on similar 13B variants on dedicated pools. hosted numbers can be similar but we can't promise the same isolation without a commit.
02:55 Priya Rao: that's encouraging. what about token/sec throughput? our worst-case load during campaign spiky windows looked like 150k tokens/sec total across the fleet.
03:10 Maya Chen: ok 150k tokens/sec aggregate. the variables are: model size (per-token compute), batching behavior, KV cache hit rate, and routing. for Redwood Dedicated, we can size the pool so that sustained throughput is covered and configure burst buffers.
03:28 Sofia Mendes: curious if the streaming implementation requires specific SDK work. we are using a websocket fanout at the edge and want to stream tokens as they come.
03:40 Jonah Patel: Redwood supports streaming responses via our API and SDKs; streaming is compatible with function/tool calling but with some nuances around chunk sizes. for websocket fanout it's just about offloading per-client fanout to your edge; Redwood streams token deltas to a single endpoint per request.
04:02 Liam Cross: any kernel/quantization recommendations? we prefer quantized models for cost but worried about latency.
04:12 Jonah Patel: quantization reduces mem and can sometimes improve latency for small models, but for streaming short sequences the kernel selection matters. our runtime auto-selects kernels based on seq len distribution. for p95 under 200ms on 13B you'll want AOQ (a quant profile) or 8-bit and dedicated GPUs tuned for low-latency preempt. we'll share recommended quant profiles in the perf guide.
04:42 Priya Rao: security question: we need SOC2 + KMS + audit logs + SSO. can hosted offer that?
04:52 Maya Chen: yes hosted is SOC2-compliant, supports SSO/SAML, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated via KMS plugins. we will attach the security packet. note: with hosted we manage keys; with dedicated/private you can integrate your KMS and get customer-managed keys.
05:12 Priya Rao: good. benchmark plan?
05:17 Jonah Patel: propose a three-step benchmark: 1) dry run on small sample prompts locally to verify correctness, 2) 30-min sustained run at 200 conc to capture steady-state p95 and throughput, 3) 15-min burst test ramping to 2k conc to observe tail behavior and fallback. we'll toggle KV cache on/off and test with and without quant profiles.
05:40 Liam Cross: that sounds solid. what metrics will you capture?
05:44 Jonah Patel: per-request p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, end-to-end edge-to-first-token latency. also memory and any OOM events.
05:57 Sofia Mendes: any network egress/residency caveats? we need EU-only for some clients.
06:03 Maya Chen: we have EU regions; for strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated in an EU region or Private. we'll note region availability in the perf doc.
06:20 Priya Rao: tradeoffs — cost vs latency — any ballpark numbers?
06:26 Maya Chen: ballpark: Hosted (shared) gives lower entry cost but higher variance; Dedicated adds a monthly reserved cost but reduces tail by ~2-3x in our benchmarks; Private has similar perf to Dedicated but adds infra and ops costs. exact numbers depend on model and quantization; we will send a cost/table showing tokens/unit with sample configs.
06:50 Liam Cross: when you say \"reduce tail 2-3x\" do you mean p95 from 600ms down to 200ms?
06:56 Jonah Patel: roughly yes for scenarios where the main cause is multi-tenant noisy neighbors. if the main cause is cold KV misses, caching strategy is the fix.
07:10 Priya Rao: ok, has Redwood done similar streaming at our scale? any customer refs?
07:16 Maya Chen: yes we have customers in comms and support with similar profiles; we can share anonymized telemetry and a reference architecture doc.
07:25 Liam Cross: curious about fallback — if Dedicated capacity is saturated during burst, what happens?
07:32 Jonah Patel: routing policy options: automated fallback to a cheaper compatible model, cross-region fallback, or queueing with degrade-to-summaries. for streaming UX, fallback to a smaller model can keep tokens flowing albeit with quality changes. we'll work with you on an acceptable policy.
07:56 Priya Rao: ok next steps?
08:00 Maya Chen: agreed actions: we'll send perf matrix + cost, Jonah will prepare benchmark script and runbook, and Hydra will share prompts. also we'll try to schedule a POC run on Dedicated or hosted depending on your infra preference.
08:12 Priya Rao: timeline: we'd like the benchmark results within two weeks to present at our Dec 8 operations review.
08:20 Maya Chen: noted; we'll aim for that.
08:27 Liam Cross: one more technical: how do you measure p95 for streaming where tokens arrive incrementally? is it per-token or per-chunk?
08:35 Jonah Patel: we give both: first-token latency and token delta latency distributions. for your SLO we'll measure time from request receive at our load balancer to the first byte to your websocket edge. you'll get p50/p95/p99 for both first-token and per-token deltas.
08:58 Sofia Mendes: any specific SDK version we should use for stream performance?
09:02 Jonah Patel: we'll include recommended SDK versions and connection tuning in the runbook. also sample consumer code for websocket fanout.
09:12 Priya Rao: great. any blockers?
09:16 Liam Cross: we need the benchmark script to support our prompt templates and to simulate our edge fanout pattern. also need clarify on data retention for logs during the test.
09:27 Maya Chen: we'll add log retention settings to the security packet; for tests we can set short retention and all logs scrubbed.
09:34 Priya Rao: perfect. thanks all.
09:37 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and scripts.
--- End transcript ---

Note on transcription: speaker labels sometimes generic; minor mis-hearings (KV cash -> KV cache).
